'''Michael Joseph Dunleavy Jr.''' (born September 15, 1980) is an American professional [[basketball]] executive and former player who is the general manager for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], earning consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors in 2002. Dunleavy was selected by Golden State with the third overall pick of the [[2002 NBA draft]]. He played in the NBA for the Warriors, [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Chicago Bulls]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He is the son of former NBA player and head coach [[Mike Dunleavy Sr.]]

==High school career==
As a 1999 graduate of [[Jesuit High School (Oregon)|Jesuit High School]] in [[Beaverton, Oregon]], Dunleavy led them to the 1999 4A State Boys Basketball Championship over [[North Salem High School (Salem, Oregon)|North Salem High School]], 65–38. Dunleavy attended the University School of Milwaukee for his freshman year, and Homestead High School in Mequon, Wisconsin for his sophomore year.

==College career==
Dunleavy played at [[Duke University]] from 1999 to 2002. As a sophomore, he played on Duke's national championship team and scored a team-high 21 points in the title game, including 3 three-pointers during a decisive 11–2 second-half Duke run. As a junior, Dunleavy was a first-team [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] All-American, averaging 17.3 points per game and 7.2 rebounds per game for the 31–4 Blue Devils.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nbadraft/tracker/player?playerId=18349|title=2002 NBA Draft: Mike Dunleavy Jr. Draft Bio|work=ESPN.com|access-date=March 29, 2010}}</ref>

In 2001–02, Dunleavy, [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]], and [[Carlos Boozer]] each scored at least 600 points for the season, a feat only matched at Duke by [[Jon Scheyer]], [[Kyle Singler]], and [[Nolan Smith]] in the 2009–10 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204918040|title=Notes: Duke 78, Baylor 71|work=GoDuke.com|date=March 28, 2010|access-date=March 29, 2010|archive-date=December 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205091943/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204918040|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Golden State Warriors (2002–2007)===
Dunleavy was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] third overall in the [[2002 NBA draft]].

In November 2005, the Warriors signed Dunleavy to a 5-year, $44 million contract extension.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dunleavy signs deal hours ahead of deadline |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2209616 |website=ESPN | date=October 31, 2005 |access-date=August 30, 2018}}</ref> During the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], Dunleavy lost his starting role as [[small forward]] for a number of games, due partly to a shooting slump. He won back the starting job later in the season and was expected to start at his new position of power forward for the 2006–07 season. Some early struggles, however, prompted Warriors head coach [[Don Nelson]] to send Dunleavy back to the bench, juggling his lineup in search of better team chemistry and winning results.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}

===Indiana Pacers (2007–2011)===
[[File:Mike Dunleavy Jr vs Bulls December 2009.jpg|thumb|Dunleavy in 2009 with Indiana]]
On January 17, 2007, Dunleavy was dealt to the [[Indiana Pacers]] along with teammates [[Troy Murphy]], [[Ike Diogu]], and [[Keith McLeod]] for [[Stephen Jackson]], [[Al Harrington]], [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]], and [[Josh Powell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mopsquad.com/artman2/publish/Indiana_Pacers_72/Pacers_Warriors_announce_8-player_deal.htm|title=Pacers, Warriors announce 8-player deal|work=MOPSquad.com|date=January 17, 2007|access-date=December 23, 2007}}</ref> In his first full season with the Pacers, Dunleavy started all 82 games and averaged a career-high 19.1 points per game.

During the 2010–2011 season, the Indiana Pacers advanced to the NBA playoffs for the first time since 2006 thanks to a regular-season finale win over the [[Washington Wizards]] coupled with a [[Charlotte Bobcats]] loss to the [[Orlando Magic]]. Dunleavy scored 14 points in the 136–112 victory.<ref>{{cite web|first=Conrad|last=Brunner|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110406/WASIND/gameinfo.html|title=Wizards-Pacers notebook|work=NBA.com|date=April 6, 2011|access-date=April 12, 2011}}</ref> Dunleavy also ended his career playoff drought of nine years and 624 games. He was the second-active leader in this category behind former Warriors and Pacers teammate Troy Murphy, who also ended his drought as a part of the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sean|last=Deveney|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2011-04-07/three-nba-players-end-long-playoff-droughts|title=Three NBA players end long playoff droughts|work=AOL.SportingNews.com|date=April 7, 2011|access-date=April 12, 2011|url-status=unfit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927052829/http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2011-04-07/three-nba-players-end-long-playoff-droughts|archive-date=September 27, 2012 }}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2011–2013)===
Following the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Dunleavy signed a two-year, $7.5 million contract with the Milwaukee Bucks on December 10.<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve|last=von Horn|url=http://www.brewhoop.com/2011/12/10/2624277/mike-dunleavy-milwaukee-bucks-signing-2011-analysis|title=Mike Dunleavy Signing: You Can Like It For 'Basketball Reasons'|work=BrewHoop.com|publisher=SB-Nation|date=December 10, 2011|access-date=December 4, 2015}}</ref> His best game as a Buck came on November 3, 2012, when he recorded 28 points and 13 rebounds against the Cleveland Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dunlemi02/gamelog/2013/|title=Mike Dunleavy 2012-13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=August 31, 2013}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2013–2016)===
On July 10, 2013, Dunleavy signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agent-guardforward-mike-dunleavy.html|title=Bulls sign free agent guard/forward Mike Dunleavy|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=August 31, 2013}}</ref> on a reported two-year deal worth about $6 million.<ref>{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Harper|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/22600695/report-mike-dunleavy-chicago-bulls-verbally-agree-to-twoyear-deal|title=Report: Mike Dunleavy, Chicago Bulls verbally agree to two-year deal|work=CBSSports.com|date=July 1, 2013|access-date=July 1, 2013}}</ref>

On April 25, 2014, Dunleavy set a playoff career-high 35 points including a franchise playoff record for most three-point field goals with 8 against the [[Washington Wizards]] in game three of their [[2014 NBA Playoffs]] first round match-up, which the Bulls won 100–97.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=White|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/bulls-beat-wizards-100-97-025437002--nba.html|title=Bulls beat Wizards 100-97, trail series 2-1|work=Sports.Yahoo.com|date=April 26, 2014|access-date=April 26, 2014|archive-date=September 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928003352/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/bulls-beat-wizards-100-97-025437002--nba.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Dunleavy injured his right ankle against the Denver Nuggets on January 1, 2015, and was sidelined for over a month.<ref>{{cite web|first=K.C.|last=Johnson|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-mike-dunleavy-bits-bulls-wizards-spt-0110-20150109-story.html|title=Bulls' Mike Dunleavy to have MRI on nagging ankle injury|work=ChicagoTribune.com|publisher=Chicago Tribune|date=January 9, 2015|access-date=January 9, 2015}}</ref>

On July 14, 2015, Dunleavy re-signed with the Bulls<ref>{{cite news|title=Bulls sign Mike Dunleavy|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-mike-dunleavy|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2015|access-date=July 14, 2015}}</ref> to a reported three-year, $14.4 million contract.<ref>{{cite news|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--mike-dunleavy-agrees-to-deal-to-return-to-bulls-094258629.html|title=Sources: Mike Dunleavy agrees to deal to return to Bulls|work=Sports.Yahoo.com|date=July 1, 2015|access-date=July 14, 2015}}</ref> After missing the Bulls' first 16 games of the season due to a back injury, he was ruled out for a further four-to-six weeks on December 3 due to the injury requiring additional rehabilitation.<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--mike-dunleavy-needs-4-to-6-weeks-before-return-to-basketball-activities-062220493.html|title=Sources: Mike Dunleavy needs 4-to-6 weeks before return to basketball activities|work=Sports.Yahoo.com|date=December 4, 2015|access-date=December 4, 2015}}</ref>

After appearing to throw punches at the Bucks' [[Michael Carter-Williams]] in a decisive game 6 in round one of the 2015 playoffs − which the Bulls won 120–66, eliminating the Bucks − [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] of the Bucks retaliated against Dunleavy's "dirty" play with a hard foul, leading to Antetokounmpo being ejected from the game. Since, Dunleavy has been perhaps the most hated current or former player among fans of the Bucks, with the vulgar initialism "FMD" being commonly used online.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Radcliffe |first1=JR |title=Moment in 2015 playoffs served as turning point for Bucks and turned Mike Dunleavy Jr. into an internet villain |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2022/04/11/since-2015-milwaukee-bucks-chicago-bulls-series-mike-dunleavy-has-been-reddit-villain/7278602001/ |access-date=14 December 2023 |agency=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]] |date=May 11, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Prince |first1=Deantae |title=Mike Dunleavy Jr. dirty fouls preceded Giannis Antetokounmpo ejection |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2015/05/01/bulls-bucks-mike-dunleavy-jr-giannis-antetokounmpo-nba-playoffs |access-date=14 December 2023 |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=May 1, 2015}}</ref>

On February 1, 2016, using the flexible assignment rule, Dunleavy was assigned to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], the [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate of the [[Golden State Warriors]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-assign-mike-dunleavy-d-league|title=Bulls Assign Mike Dunleavy to D-League|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2016|access-date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> with the goal to practice there during the Bulls' West Coast road trip.<ref>{{cite web|first=Marc J.|last=Spears|url=https://twitter.com/SpearsNBAYahoo/status/694322893920952320|title=Ex-Warrior Mike Dunleavy will practice but won't...|work=Twitter|date=February 1, 2016|access-date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he was recalled by the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-recall-dunleavy-santa-cruz-warriors|title=BULLS RECALL DUNLEAVY FROM THE SANTA CRUZ WARRIORS|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2016|access-date=February 3, 2016}}</ref> On February 6, Dunleavy made his season debut for the Bulls after missing the first 49 games. He played 14 minutes and scored five points in a 112–105 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Krawczynski|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160206/CHIMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Timberwolves close out Bulls with 12-0 run to win 112-105|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2016|access-date=February 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303191113/http://www.nba.com/games/20160206/CHIMIN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 3, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2016–2017)===
On July 7, 2016, Dunleavy was traded, along with the rights to [[Vladimir Veremeenko]], to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for the rights to [[Albert Miralles]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/dunleavy-trade-160707|title=Cavaliers Acquire Forward Mike Dunleavy From Chicago|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Cavaliers in the team's season opener on October 25, 2016, against the [[New York Knicks]]. In 22 minutes off the bench, he recorded four points, four rebounds, two assists and three steals in a 117–88 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899375|title=Knicks vs. Cavaliers – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 25, 2016|access-date=October 25, 2016}}</ref> On December 23, 2016, he scored a season-high 14 points in a 119–99 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899886|title=James, Love lead Cavs to 119-99 rout of Nets; Warriors next|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2016|access-date=December 23, 2016}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2017)===
On January 7, 2017, Dunleavy was traded, along with [[Mo Williams]] and a future first-round draft pick, to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Kyle Korver]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-first-round-pick-dunleavy-williams-cavs-kyle-korver|title=Hawks Acquire First Round Pick, Dunleavy & Williams From Cavs For Kyle Korver|work=NBA.com|date=January 7, 2017|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref> After Dunleavy initially refused to report to the Hawks while seeking a buyout of his contract, he changed his mind and agreed to join the team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Pollakoff|first=Brett|url=http://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/mike-dunleavy-changes-mind-reportedly-agrees-join-hawks-trade-cavaliers-010917|title=Mike Dunleavy changes his mind, reportedly agrees to join Hawks after trade from Cavaliers|work=FoxSports.com|date=January 9, 2017|access-date=January 10, 2017}}</ref> On January 10, he reported to the team and passed his physical.<ref>{{cite web|last=Vivlamore|first=Chris|url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/basketball/dunleavy-reports-hawks-passes-physical/Hle4MZDbOosnWLwcH9FrQM/|title=Dunleavy Jr. reports to Hawks, passes physical|work=AJC.com|date=January 10, 2017|access-date=January 10, 2017}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut for the Hawks, scoring six points on a pair of three-pointers in a 103–101 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900018|title=Thomas steadies Celtics, Horford triumphant in return home|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2017|access-date=January 14, 2017}}</ref> On January 15, he scored 20 points off the bench in a 111–98 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. It was his first 20-point performance since a first-round playoff game for Chicago on April 30, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900028|title=Bazemore, Dunleavy pick up offense, Hawks beat Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=January 15, 2017}}</ref> On March 3, 2017, Dunleavy was diagnosed with right ankle [[synovitis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/dunleavy-out-right-ankle-injury|title=Dunleavy Out With Right Ankle Injury|work=NBA.com|date=March 3, 2017|access-date=March 3, 2017}}</ref> He returned to action on March 22 against Washington after a 13-game injury layoff.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900458|title=Beal, Wall lead Wizards to 104-100 win over Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=March 22, 2017|access-date=March 23, 2017}}</ref>

Dunleavy's final NBA game was Game 6 of the 2017 Eastern Conference First Round on April 28, 2017, in a 99–115 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]]. In his final game, Dunleavy only played for 71 seconds, substituting towards the end of the first quarter for Tim Hardaway Jr.. He would subsequently sit out the rest of the game, as the Hawks went on to lose the game and the series to Washington 4–2. On June 30, 2017, he was waived by the Hawks, and retired shortly afterwards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-waive-mike-dunleavy|title=Hawks Waive Mike Dunleavy|work=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2017|access-date=June 30, 2017}}</ref>

==Executive career==
On September 24, 2018, Dunleavy was hired by the [[Golden State Warriors]] as a pro scout.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/basketball-operations-promotions-additions-20180924|title=Warriors Announce Promotions and Additions to Basketball Operations Staff|work=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2018|access-date=September 24, 2018}}</ref>  On August 29, 2019, Dunleavy was promoted to assistant general manager of the Warriors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://balldurham.com/2019/09/03/mike-dunleavy-named-golden-state-warriors-assistant-gm/|title=Mike Dunleavy named as Golden State Warriors Assistant GM|date=2019-09-04|website=Ball Durham|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-23}}</ref> On September 30, 2021, Dunleavy was promoted to vice president of basketball operations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2021/9/30/22703034/warriors-promotions-basketball-operations-mike-dunleavy-jr-zaza-pachula |title=Warriors announce various basketball operations hirings and promotions|work=GoldenStateOfMind.com|date=September 30, 2021|access-date=September 30, 2021}}</ref> He won his first [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] after the Warriors defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] in six games in the [[2022 NBA Finals]]. On June 16, 2023, Dunleavy was promoted to general manager of the Warriors following [[Bob Myers]]' subsequent step down from the position.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Viray |first1=Joe |title=Mike Dunleavy Jr. is the Warriors' new General Manager |url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2023/6/16/23763332/warriors-news-mike-dunleavy-jr-general-manager |access-date=17 June 2023 |date=June 16, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Klopfer |first=Brady |date=2023-06-13 |title=The Warriors seem in no rush to name a GM |url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2023/6/13/23760202/warriors-gm-bob-myers-mike-dunleavy-jr-joe-lacob-kirk-lacob |access-date=2023-07-03 |website=Golden State Of Mind |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dunleavy has two younger brothers: [[Baker Dunleavy|Baker]], who played at [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] from 2002 to 2006 and is the former head coach at [[Quinnipiac Bobcats men's basketball|Quinnipiac]];<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/article/quinnipiac-basketball-coach-resign-villanova-17894924.php | title=Quinnipiac men's basketball coach Baker Dunleavy resigns, assistant Tom Pecora named head coach | date=April 13, 2023 }}</ref> and James, who was a walk-on for [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and is currently an NBA player agent. His father is [[Mike Dunleavy Sr.]], former [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and Portland Trail Blazers coach, retired NBA player, and the former head coach at [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]]. While growing up, Dunleavy attended a residential sports camp in Eagle River, Wisconsin called Camp Menominee. In 2008, Camp Menominee honored Dunleavy by naming its basketball courts "The Mike Dunleavy Jr. Courts".{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}
